claims.text: The Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are initially solid and chemically homogeneous.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity governs the premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Thermal activation drives Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
Cu is a lower-melting constituent relative to the other elements in the stated alloy.
Heating increases atomic mobility in the nanoparticles.
Cu atoms interact relatively weakly in this alloy system.
The relatively weak interactions and low melting point of Cu cause Cu atoms to segregate to the surface during heating.
Surface Cu enrichment creates localized regions with reduced melting temperatures.
The Cu-enriched regions initiate heterogeneous surface premelting.
Localized premelting propagates through the particle until the entire nanoparticle melts as heating continues.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles will exhibit earlier surface premelting than more homogeneous or chemically simpler nanoparticles.
The spatial onset of premelting will correlate with Cu-enriched surface regions.
Single-metal or bimetallic baseline nanoparticles have less pronounced surface segregation and chemical complexity.
The proposed mechanism applies to nanoparticles of similar size and multielement composition under oxidation-suppressing atmospheres.
The mechanism may not apply to bulk materials or nanoparticles whose surfaces have been substantially altered by extrinsic treatments.
The magnitude of the temperature shift and melting heterogeneity may vary with particle size and synthesis details.
Standard synthesis produces nanoparticles with an as-synthesized chemically heterogeneous surface.
Post-treatment by annealing or mechanical processing can produce a more uniform elemental distribution for the control particles.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as chemically homogeneous, whereas the standard as-synthesized particles in the falsification experiment are described as having a chemically heterogeneous surface. It is unclear whether these are intended to be the same baseline material.
